text: α-Catenin acts as a tension transducer that induces adherens junction (AJ) development. AJs, organized by adhesion proteins and the actin cytoskeleton, likely sense pulling forces from adjacent cells and modulate opposing forces to maintain tissue integrity, but the regulatory mechanism was unknown. Rather than acting as a direct membrane–actin linker, α-catenin recruits vinculin, another main AJ actin-binding protein, via force-dependent changes in α-catenin conformation. The authors identified α-catenin regions required for this force-dependent vinculin binding using mutant α-catenin introduced into cells and in vitro binding assays. Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) analysis of α-catenin mobility, plus an antibody recognizing α-catenin in a force-dependent manner, supported the conclusion that α-catenin translates mechanical stimuli into a chemical response, driving AJ development.
